reference_sql:
SELECT product_id, category_id, launch_date,
  launch_date - LAG(launch_date) OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY launch_date, product_id) AS days_after_prev
FROM products
WHERE category_id IN (1, 2)
  AND launch_date IS NOT NULL
alternatives:
SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date,
  p.launch_date - (SELECT MAX(p2.launch_date) FROM products p2
    WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id
      AND (p2.launch_date < p.launch_date OR (p2.launch_date = p.launch_date AND p2.product_id < p.product_id))) AS days_after_prev
FROM products p
WHERE p.category_id IN (1, 2)
  AND p.launch_date IS NOT NULL

SELECT product_id, category_id, launch_date,
  date_diff('day', LAG(launch_date) OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY launch_date, product_id), launch_date) AS days_after_prev
FROM products
WHERE category_id IN (1, 2)
  AND launch_date IS NOT NULL

other_way.sql:
SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date,
  p.launch_date - (SELECT MAX(p2.launch_date) FROM products p2
    WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id
      AND (p2.launch_date < p.launch_date OR (p2.launch_date = p.launch_date AND p2.product_id < p.product_id))) AS days_after_prev
FROM products p
WHERE p.category_id IN (1, 2)
  AND p.launch_date IS NOT NULL
other_way.tradeoff: The latest earlier launch from a subquery gives the same days, but the same-day tie rule has to be written out by hand.
